reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as an instructional Coinbase walkthrough covering account assets, a Bitcoin purchase preview, Learn and Earn lessons, and yield features. The referral-linked rewards and cryptocurrency participation steps are described as stated offers and tutorial explanations, without deception or completed losses. A separate automation-related promotion is partially garbled and treated as an uncertain additional offer rather than evidence of a different mechanism.

go to the description, click the link then you will go to the Coinbase sign-up page

opening.argument: The video ties a concrete crypto reward to a viewer's financial action through the creator's signup route. Viewers are told to use the link, buy approximately $100 of cryptocurrency, and receive $10 in Bitcoin. The same presentation also asks viewers to invite acquaintances, with another $100 purchase condition linked to a Bitcoin reward. This is not merely general education: it gives the audience a direct registration-and-purchase path for obtaining digital assets, while the creator benefits from directing participation through referral links.

after they join coinbase when one joins coinbase and they earn $100 worth of of cryptocurrency They buy or sell $100 worth of cryptocurrency and they receive $10 worth as free bitcoin
Since you refered to them you can receive $10 dollar of Free Bitcoin from Coinbase

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a walkthrough does not answer the central solicitation. The walkthrough repeatedly turns instructions into a reward pathway: use the link, buy or sell the stated amount, and receive Bitcoin. The fact that the offer is attributed to Coinbase does not remove the video's role in directing viewers to register and transact, and the opening does not address the creator's additional referral benefit.

citations.quote: go to the description, click the link then you will go to the Coinbase sign-up page
you can receive $10 dollar of Free Bitcoin from Coinbase

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited material describes a stated Coinbase referral promotion, not an invented giveaway or a promise that everyone receives money without conditions. The condition is explicit: the referred person must join and buy or sell the specified amount. The opening also shows that the video explains the Coinbase interface and purchase process, so a referral-linked offer does not by itself establish a scam.

opening.argument: The video presents staking as a simple route from acquiring or converting crypto to passive yield. It instructs viewers to buy Cosmos, place it into the yield feature, and says the result can earn 5% APY; it also explains converting Bitcoin into Cosmos before staking. The screen reinforces this with a visible yield figure and a 37-day typical hold time. That combination of a specified annual return, a required crypto purchase or conversion, and a hold period is a material investment solicitation, not just neutral platform navigation.

citations.quote: You can earn 5% annual percentage yield as interest.
you can now invest here to earn a 5% annual percentage yield.
when it already starts earning, we can earn up to 5% annual percentage yield

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening treats the yield figure as an ordinary feature explanation, but that misses the actionable sequence. Viewers are told how to acquire the asset, convert existing Bitcoin, and put it into yield, while the presentation highlights the return. Explaining a platform's buttons does not make a return-linked staking pitch non-promotional.

citations.quote: you would put Cosmos and pay with what your debit cards or credit cards that you want to use

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The return language is qualified as an available yield feature, not presented as a guaranteed profit or deception. The cited explanation says the rate depends on which assets are available, and the interface identifies a typical hold time, allowing viewers to see the relevant terms. Describing how to buy or convert an asset before using a platform feature is consistent with operational education.

opening.argument: The tutorial framing functions as a distribution channel for several participation offers. The description directs viewers to register with multiple cryptocurrency services and pairs those destinations with commission, rewards, or free Bitcoin. The video also ends by explicitly telling viewers to use the links in the description, while a separate pitch directs interested people to click through and complete a form for a claimed complete-autopilot crypto opportunity. These calls to action show that the instructional wrapper is steering viewers toward external signups and forms, not simply teaching concepts.

citations.quote: Register on Binance and get 10% commission
Register on Coinspot get $10 Bitcoin
who would like to learn how you can make 100% crypto a complete autopilot
click nalang young bottom complete this form

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference response narrows the video to the Coinbase screen demonstrations and calls the other pitch uncertain, but that leaves out the explicit conversion of viewers into link users. The end card asks viewers to use the description links, and the description lists multiple reward-bearing registrations. Even if one segment is unclear, the plainly stated external calls to action remain part of the video's function.

citations.quote: Register on Binance and get 10% commission
Register on Coinspot get $10 Bitcoin

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The evidence supports promotional links, but promotion alone does not establish a scam. The main spoken purpose is explicitly a beginner Coinbase tutorial, and the external offers are identified as registration benefits rather than hidden claims that the creator controls viewers' funds. The autopilot passage is partly garbled and does not establish what users would receive or lose, so it cannot carry the stronger conclusion.
